variants.headline: Looking back: grant programme passes over needy districts
variants.sub: Districts in need were passed over by a government grant programme.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: A government grant programme had passed over districts that needed it.

Labour's question is plain: whose need counts when public support is shared out? Districts in need should not vanish behind the language of a programme. Working people deserve allocation judged by its purpose, without an invented story about who personally benefited or what a particular household was denied.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We support {target} against a wider verdict built on assumption. The allocation defect deserves attention, but it does not prove every accusation about motives or justify an invented account of private favour.

variants.headline: Looking back: need goes unanswered in grant allocation

variants.headline: Looking back: government grants miss the districts in need
variants.sub: A government grant programme has passed over districts that needed it.
variants.body:
The headline belongs to {first_reported}. Our original account recorded this: A government grant allocation had overlooked the districts that needed support.

Labour's question is plain: whose need counts when public support is shared out? Districts in need should not vanish behind the language of a programme. Working people deserve allocation judged by its purpose, without an invented story about who personally benefited or what a particular household was denied.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.

We support {target} against a wider verdict built on assumption. The allocation defect deserves attention, but it does not prove every accusation about motives or justify an invented account of private favour.
